encodingDesc.p: Printed small capitals transcribed in uppercase; ordinary line-wrap hyphenation joined explicitly; lexical hyphens, spelling, punctuation, brackets and printed footnote pointers retained. Raw digital HTML/XML, scan crops and source bytes remain recoverable. Comparisons may fold case and ae/æ; original source readings are retained without such folding.

normalization.p: Sentence-case presentation is an editorial layer, not a replacement transcription. Each choice retains the exact accepted 1856 text in orig and a case-only display in reg. Proper names, ligatures, punctuation, spelling, source pointers and Roman labels are preserved; common nouns are lowercased. Compiled-index CSS selects reg only, without altering other witnesses.

revisionDesc.change: Authorized human browser-review correction: one provenance note immediately below the index title; reversible sentence-case readings and left-aligned presentation. Original 1856 readings and existing structural identities remain intact.

div.head: Whiston’s chapter headings (compiled index)
div.note: Compiled from the chapter headings printed in the Auburn and Rochester edition of Whiston's translation (Alden & Beardsley, 1856). The arrangement as an index is editorial, not an original printed table of contents.

choice.orig: CONTAINING THE INTERVAL OF EIGHTEEN YEARS.
choice.reg: Containing the interval of eighteen years.

choice.orig: FROM THE DEATH OF ANTIGONUS TO THE FINISHING OF THE TEMPLE BY HEROD.
choice.reg: From the death of Antigonus to the finishing of the temple by Herod.

choice.orig: CONCERNING POLLIO AND SAMEAS. HEROD SLAYS THE PRINCIPAL OF ANTIGONUS'S FRIENDS, AND SPOILS THE CITY OF ITS WEALTH. ANTONY BEHEADS ANTIGONUS.
choice.reg: Concerning Pollio and Sameas. Herod slays the principal of Antigonus's friends, and spoils the city of its wealth. Antony beheads Antigonus.

choice.orig: HOW HYRCANUS WAS SET AT LIBERTY BY THE PARTHIANS, AND RETURNED TO HEROD; AND WHAT ALEXANDRA DID WHEN SHE HEARD THAT ANANELUS WAS MADE HIGH-PRIEST.
choice.reg: How Hyrcanus was set at liberty by the Parthians, and returned to Herod; and what Alexandra did when she heard that Ananelus was made high-priest.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD, UPON HIS MAKING ARISTOBULUS HIGH-PRIEST, TOOK CARE THAT HE SHOULD BE MURDERED IN A LITTLE TIME; AND WHAT APOLOGY HE MADE TO ANTONY ABOUT ARISTOBULUS: AS ALSO CONCERNING JOSEPH AND MARIAMNE.
choice.reg: How Herod, upon his making Aristobulus high-priest, took care that he should be murdered in a little time; and what apology he made to Antony about Aristobulus: as also concerning Joseph and Mariamne.

choice.orig: HOW CLEOPATRA, WHEN SHE HAD GOTTEN FROM ANTONY SOME PARTS OF JUDEA AND ARABIA, CAME INTO JUDEA; AND HOW HEROD GAVE HER MANY PRESENTS, AND CONDUCTED HER ON HER WAY BACK TO EGYPT.
choice.reg: How Cleopatra, when she had gotten from Antony some parts of Judea and Arabia, came into Judea; and how Herod gave her many presents, and conducted her on her way back to Egypt.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD MADE WAR WITH THE KING OF ARABIA, AND AFTER THEY HAD FOUGHT MANY BATTLES, AT LENGTH CONQUERED HIM, AND WAS CHOSEN BY THE ARABS TO BE GOVERNOR OF THAT NATION; AS ALSO CONCERNING A GREAT EARTHQUAKE.
choice.reg: How Herod made war with the king of Arabia, and after they had fought many battles, at length conquered him, and was chosen by the Arabs to be governor of that nation; as also concerning a great earthquake.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD SLEW HYRCANUS, AND THEN HASTED AWAY TO CÆSAR, AND OBTAINED THE KINGDOM FROM HIM ALSO; AND HOW, A LITTLE TIME AFTERWARD, HE ENTERTAINED CÆSAR IN A MOST HONOURABLE MANNER.
choice.reg: How Herod slew Hyrcanus, and then hasted away to Cæsar, and obtained the kingdom from him also; and how, a little time afterward, he entertained Cæsar in a most honourable manner.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD SLEW SOHEMUS AND MARIAMNE, AND AFTERWARDS ALEXANDRA AND COSTOBARUS, AND HIS MOST INTIMATE FRIENDS, AND, AT LAST, THE SONS OF BABA ALSO.
choice.reg: How Herod slew Sohemus and Mariamne, and afterwards Alexandra and Costobarus, and his most intimate friends, and, at last, the sons of Baba also.

choice.orig: HOW TEN MEN OF THE CITIZENS [OF JERUSALEM] MADE A CONSPIRACY AGAINST HEROD, FOR THE FOREIGN PRACTICES HE HAD INTRODUCED, WHICH WAS A TRANSGRESSION OF THE LAWS OF THEIR COUNTRY. CONCERNING THE BUILDING OF SEBASTE AND CÆSAREA, AND OTHER EDIFICES OF HEROD.
choice.reg: How ten men of the citizens [of Jerusalem] made a conspiracy against Herod, for the foreign practices he had introduced, which was a transgression of the laws of their country. Concerning the building of Sebaste and Cæsarea, and other edifices of Herod.

choice.orig: CONCERNING THE FAMINE THAT HAPPENED IN JUDEA AND SYRIA; AND HOW HEROD, AFTER HE HAD MARRIED ANOTHER WIFE, REBUILT CÆSAREA, AND OTHER GRECIAN CITIES.
choice.reg: Concerning the famine that happened in Judea and Syria; and how Herod, after he had married another wife, rebuilt Cæsarea, and other Grecian cities.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD SENT HIS SONS TO ROME; HOW ALSO HE WAS ACCUSED BY ZENODORUS AND THE GADARENS, BUT WAS CLEARED OF WHAT THEY ACCUSED HIM OF, AND WITHAL GAINED TO HIMSELF THE GOOD-WILL OF CÆSAR. CONCERNING THE PHARISEES, THE ESSENS, AND MANAHEM.
choice.reg: How Herod sent his sons to Rome; how also he was accused by Zenodorus and the Gadarens, but was cleared of what they accused him of, and withal gained to himself the good-will of Cæsar. Concerning the Pharisees, the Essens, and Manahem.

choice.orig: HOW HEROD REBUILT THE TEMPLE, AND RAISED IT HIGHER, AND MADE IT MORE MAGNIFICENT THAN IT WAS BEFORE; AND ALSO CONCERNING THAT TOWER WHICH HE CALLED ANTONIA.
choice.reg: How Herod rebuilt the temple, and raised it higher, and made it more magnificent than it was before; and also concerning that tower which he called Antonia.
